boundary: NIFC final fire perimeter (research/fires/aspen-acres.geojson; web perimeter layer). NISAR burn layer frames 2026-06-03/06-15/06-27 are pre-fire; first post-fire frame 2026-07-09. Only ~23% of in-perimeter pixels exceed burn 0.3 by 2026-08-26, so NISAR's scar is patchy inside the Beulah valley (grass/ponderosa understory burns and 120 m mixing with unburned lots).

items.title: Historic Horseshoe Lodge destroyed, Pueblo Mountain Park
items.place: Horseshoe Lodge, NWDC Mountain Campus, 9112 Pueblo Mountain Park Rd, Beulah, Pueblo County, CO
items.what_it_shows: The roofless, gutted 1930s lodge (community hub for school visits, 4-H camps, art shows) with blackened ponderosa pines around it, photographed on the 10 July 2026 media tour.
items.credit: Mike Sweeney, Special to The Colorado Sun
items.notes: Loss confirmed by The Colorado Sun, Denver7 (Sheriff David Lucero) and Wikipedia. Coordinates are the OSM node for the NWDC Mountain Campus, which includes the Horseshoe Lodge & Retreat Center (visitpueblo.org); the lodge itself may be up to ~150 m away. A second lodge photo is Colo_Sun_Beulah_Tour_05.jpg.

items.title: Home burned to its foundation on South Pine Drive
items.place: South Pine Drive, Valley View, Beulah, Pueblo County, CO
items.what_it_shows: A bare concrete foundation where a house stood, photographed 10 July 2026. The same story describes the arbitrary pattern along South Pine Drive: one home reduced to ash, another untouched just feet away; two cars melted into molten metal (Colo_Sun_Beulah_Tour_04.jpg).
items.credit: Mike Sweeney, Special to The Colorado Sun
items.notes: Street-level location only (Nominatim centroid of South Pine Drive); the exact house is not identified. The street runs ~1 km, so the pin is good to a few hundred metres. Because it mixes destroyed and surviving homes, this is a good place for the 'edge pixels are mixed' caveat.

items.title: Downtown Beulah still standing: Beulah Inn, coffee shop, general store, post office
items.place: Central Beulah (Pennsylvania Ave area), Pueblo County, CO; pin at Beulah Community Center
items.what_it_shows: Story, no photo: Beulah Fire spokesperson Jill Laca says the downtown, 'another heart of Beulah', survived, including the historic Beulah Inn, coffee shop, general store and post office, while the lodge 2.6 km south was lost.
items.credit: The Colorado Sun (reporting); Wikipedia also states 'the center part of the towns were not affected'
items.notes: Pin is the OSM Beulah Community Center (next to the United Methodist Church at 38.07284,-104.98910) as a proxy for the small downtown; the named businesses are within a few hundred metres but were not geocoded individually (not in OSM). Best 'saved' counterpart to the Horseshoe Lodge and South Pine Drive items.

items.title: Greenwood ringed by fireline and saved
items.place: Greenwood, Custer County, CO (CO-96 / CR 395 area)
items.what_it_shows: Story, no photo: on 5–6 July outflow winds pushed the fire north toward Greenwood and Wetmore. Crews worked through the night, built a fireline around Greenwood and finished a bulldozer firebreak south of Wetmore. The fire stopped short of both.
items.notes: Pin is the Nominatim hamlet node for Greenwood (a dispersed rural community, so ±500 m). Wetmore (38.2385,-105.0850) is at v=0.008, almost at the top edge of the hero grid, 3.9 km outside the perimeter.

items.title: Rye town centre spared while outskirts burned
items.place: Rye, Pueblo County, CO (Main St / CO-165)
items.what_it_shows: Story, no photo: Rye was fully evacuated on 2–3 July when the fire's head jumped roads toward Colorado City and Rye. Homes on the outskirts of Beulah and Rye were damaged or destroyed, but the town centres were not.
items.notes: Weakest source: Wikipedia's 'outskirts burned, centre not affected' line cites Watch Duty. A search summary claimed '28 homes destroyed in Rye', but I could not verify that on any fetched page, so it is not used. I found no named Rye street with losses.
